title: Safer Terraform CI for Private/VPC: canary workspaces, module upgrade safety, policy-evaluator
creator: Alex Moreno
description: Add a hardened CI/CD workflow for Private (VPC) Terraform modules that reduces risk during module upgrades and keeps customer VPCs healthy. This covers linting, plan/apply pipelines, canary pre-apply workspaces, automated module bump PRs, policy-as-code enforcement, and runtime drift detection health checks.
background: Private deployments run customer VPCs and tenant isolation components. Past incidents show that module upgrades and misconfigured TF can introduce network regressions. We need a repeatable pipeline that provides: automated safety checks, a low-risk canary path before full rollout, and continuous drift detection after applies.
proposed_solution: 1) Create a standardized CI pipeline template (GitHub Actions) that runs formatting, static checks (tflint), security scanning (tfsec/scan), and terraform plan. 2) Implement a 'canary workspace' flow: module-bump PRs open a canary workspace that performs an apply against an isolated sandbox account/namespace; automated smoke tests run; on success the pipeline opens a staged rollout PR to apply to a small set of production-like seats. 3) Implement a policy-evaluator service in the mono-repo that consumes Rego rules from a policy-registry and returns structured failures; the CI job fails plan if critical rules block (e.g., public ip on subnet, missing flow logs). 4) Add drift detection: daily plan-based drift checks against remote state with automatic detection of unauthorized changes; critical drifts create PagerDuty alerts and create remediation PRs. 5) Ship reusable module-versioning automation (dependabot-style) that opens PRs with module bumps and attaches a generated plan and risk score. 6) Document rollback and escalation playbooks and wire alerts into the Console and runbooks.
tasks: Create github-actions/ci-terraform-template with jobs: format, lint (tflint), static-security (tfsec), plan, policy-eval
Design and implement canary workspace runner using isolated cloud accounts and a sandbox TF workspace template
Build policy-evaluator: Rego rules in infra/policies, action that evaluates plan JSON and returns failures
Add module-bump bot configuration to terraform-modules repo (auto PR generation, include plan artifacts)
Implement drift-check job scheduled daily that runs terraform plan against remote state and files an incident PR on unexpected diffs
Wire policy-eval results into PR checks with human-friendly error messages and suggested fixes
Create runbook: canary criteria, rollout blast radius, automated rollback steps, and PagerDuty escalation
Add observability: plan latency, rate of blocked plans, canary success/failure metrics to Console dashboards
acceptance_criteria: CI template lives in infra/.github/workflows and can be consumed by module repos via workflow_call
Module-bump PRs created by bot include a generated plan artifact and an automated risk score
Canary workspace flow can perform a full apply in sandbox and run smoke tests; documented example exists
Policy-evaluator blocks plans that violate critical security/network rules and returns clear remediation hints
Drift-check job runs daily, opens remediation PRs for 90% of detectable unauthorized diffs in staging, and pages on critical drift
At least one end-to-end run using the new pipeline is recorded (PR -> canary apply -> staged rollout -> monitor) with postmortem and lessons learned
Runbook and playbook reviewed and signed off by Security and SRE
dependencies: remote-state locking (backend config) must be standardized across modules
sandbox account with isolated permissions for canary applies
PagerDuty escalation policy for drift/failed-canary alerts
Module registry versioning conventions (semver) agreed with platform team
notes: We should avoid coupling the policy-evaluator implementation to a specific runner; expose a lightweight CLI that GH Actions can invoke so it is portable.
Risk scoring heuristic: combine changed resource count, replacement count, and presence of network-surface changes to compute a simple red/yellow/green score
Consider a future extension to allow scheduled automatic applies for low-risk module bumps (opt-in per customer)
This ticket intentionally avoids prescribing a single scanning tool; use combination of tflint, tfsec and optionally checkov where coverage gaps exist
